notes.decision: Chapter title spread across lines 23-26 in decorated layout with Ⲟ markers. 'Concerning the body, that it was established with respect to the likeness of the cosmos.' The microcosm-macrocosm correspondence is the topic: the human body IS in the likeness of the cosmos. ⲥⲙⲛⲧϩ = ⲥⲙⲟⲛⲧ̄ (qualitative of ⲥⲙⲓⲛⲉ 'establish'). ⲟⲩⲃⲉ here = 'with respect to, against (in correspondence with).'
Standard Manichaean narrative formula 'on one of the occasions/times.' ⲟⲩⲉ ⲛ̄ⲛⲥⲏⲩ = 'one of the times.'
'Assembly' — per accumulated vocabulary. The Apostle teaches in the church (ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ) in the midst of the assembled congregation.

Translated 'his head' (ⲧⲉϩ- Lyc. feminine possessive 'his' + ⲁⲁⲡⲉ 'head,' cf. accumulated ⲡⲁⲁⲡⲉ 'head/sheaf'). The whole page maps body parts to cosmic regions, all governed by Lyc. possessive ⲡⲉϩ-/ⲛⲉϩ-/ⲧⲉϩ-.

Translated 'the firstfruit of the five garments' — Greek ἀπαρχή (in glossary as 'firstfruits') + ⲧϯⲉ '(the) five' + ⲍⲃⲥⲱ 'garments' (cf. accumulated ⲧϣⲁⲙⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲍⲃⲥⲱ 'three garments' for Living Spirit). The five garments here likely = the five storehouses/elements. The head corresponds to the cosmic apex from which the five-element system is set forth.

Rendered 'the wheel of the sphere that sows.' ⲥⲓⲧⲉ = standard Coptic 'sow, scatter.' In Manichaean cosmology the cosmic wheel-sphere is associated with the sowing/scattering of zodiacal forms onto creation. The qualitative-relative form ⲉⲧⲥⲓⲧⲉ identifies the wheel as actively sowing.

Translated tentatively 'his shins' (the body part between knees and feet, fitting the descending body-mapping sequence: knees → ⲛⲥⲛϩⲉ → soles-of-feet). Likely related to accumulated tentative ⲛⲉⲩⲥⲛⲩⲉ 'their legs.' Could alternatively be 'his (two) bonds/cords.' Confidence moderate.
Rendered 'the soles of his feet.' ⲟⲩⲱⲡ/ⲟⲁⲡ = 'sole of foot' (Crum); ⲣⲉⲧϥ̄ = 'his feet.' The mapping (sole onto 'this earth' beneath which Omophoros stands) confirms the foot-bottom reading.

Translated 'his liver' as Lyc. reflex of Greek ἧπαρ (cf. accumulated ⲡⲉϩⲍⲏⲡⲁⲣ 'his liver' from elsewhere in the corpus). The ⲧ in ⲍⲏⲧⲁⲣ instead of expected ⲡ in ⲍⲏⲡⲁⲣ is unusual — likely a scribal slip ⲧ for ⲡ, or a Lycopolitan orthographic variant. The body-element mapping (liver → fire-stronghold; flesh → darkness; sinew → water) is well-attested Manichaean.

Translated 'his sinew.' ⲥⲛⲁϩ from ⲥⲛⲁϩ 'bind' = 'bond, sinew, cord' — in body-anatomical context, the binding-tissue. The mapping to water-stronghold is consistent with Manichaean correspondence schemes where vessels/sinews carry vital fluid.

Translated tentatively 'his stations.' The lexeme ⲧⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉⲩⲉ is unattested in our glossary. Context places it within the cosmic-architectural inventory (firmaments / hosts / X / preparations / strongholds) — suggesting some structural cosmic locus. Possibly related to ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise' = 'risings/ascensions' or to a watch/post-noun. Confidence low.

Translated 'the great King.' ⲡⲛⲁⲩ here functions as a Lyc. variant of ⲛⲁϭ/ⲛⲁⲟ/ⲛⲁⲃ 'great' (the standard Manichaean title is 'the Great King of Honor,' cf. accumulated ⲡⲛⲁⲃ ⲛ̄ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲟ). Same form recurs at line 28 in identical pattern.

Rendered tentatively 'there.' The form ⲙ̄ⲙⲁϩ recurs at line 30 in the same role as a discourse-locative. Likely a Lycopolitan orthographic variant of ⲙⲙⲁⲩ 'there' (with epenthetic/orthographic ϩ for ⲩ — a known Lyc. dialectal feature). Confidence moderate.

Rendered 'I shall reveal to you forth' as 1sg present-future of ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄ 'reveal' with ⲛⲏⲧⲛ̄ 'to you' and ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' The reduction ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄ for ϯⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄ / ⲧⲣⲁⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ̄ is dialectal. The pair 'I have revealed... once again I shall reveal' frames the leer-break as transition between two expositions.

Translated 'the King — from the firmament unto below he stands fast' — preserving the spatial-cosmological reach of the King's authority from upper firmament down to the four lower lands. The structure introduces the five-watch schema that follows.

Restored 'fifth' rather than another ordinal because the kephalaion enumerates exactly five watches; line 4 has 'fourth' (King of Glory's watch over the three wheels), and the next ordinal ('fifth') logically belongs to the Omophoros. The single missing character ϯ fits Lyc. ⲙⲁϩϯⲉ.

Read as 'as also a lord' — Greek ὡς + ⲛ̄ϩⲟⲛ ('as') + ⲛ̄ⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲥ ('a lord') with reinforcing ⲁⲛ. The Omophoros holds authority not merely as bearer but also as sovereign over the great middle land — a doubled cosmic title.

Translated 'the four extremities' — ⲧⲱϭⲥ̄ likely means 'limbs/extremities/joints' here; in context with 'at his feet' these are the four lower lands set beneath the great middle land. Corresponds antithetically to the three lands on the head.

The summary line 'in the five watches each at its season' wraps the cosmic-temporal framework before launching into the per-watch description (lines 12ff). The 'season' (ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ϣ ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ϣ) means 'each at its proper time.'

ⲭⲉϩⲁⲃⲉⲃⲉ parsed as infinitive of a verb of bubbling/gushing-up (cf. ⲃⲉⲃⲉ 'gush forth' in glossary). 'Sin sought to gush up against the icon of the Ambassador' fits the Manichaean motif of dark substance straining upward toward the Third Ambassador's revealed image and being repelled.

notes.decision: Identification: 'the great King of Honor, that is the Egregoroi.' This is striking — typically the King of Honor is a single hypostasis (in glossary). Here he is glossed as the Watchers (Egregoroi). Possibly an exegetical equation specific to this passage: in the King of Honor's watch, the Egregoroi-event takes place (their descent and binding by the four angels).
Read as ⲧⲟⲩ-ⲫⲃⲓⲁⲩ from ⲫⲃⲟ 'subdue, vanquish' (in glossary). 'Until they were subdued' fits the Manichaean myth of the Egregoroi's binding by the four angels after their descent.
The form ⲁⲩⲕⲓⲛⲏⲥⲓⲥ (with restored ⲁ) reflects Lyc. indefinite-article ⲁⲩ for ⲟⲩ before the Greek loanword κίνησις 'motion.' Standard Manichaean term for cosmic disturbance.

ⲏⲙⲙⲁϩⲉ tentatively parsed as a verbal noun on ⲉⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp, exercise authority' — 'this grasping/seizure'; ⲥⲱϩⲧ qualitative of ⲥⲁϩⲧ̄ 'weave, intertwine.' Together: 'this seizure was woven together with the rising-up of the three wheels' — the King of Glory's authority over the wheels operates as an integrated cosmic-mechanical event. Confidence low; alternative readings possible.

ⲕⲱϩ taken as 'stretch out' (Crum); 'they stretched out their bonds' — describes the Omophoros's lower extremities (the four lands at his feet) drying up and their fastenings being pulled taut, producing the great earthquake. Could alternatively mean 'kindled' or 'were jealous-of'; spatial sense fits best.

ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲧⲟⲗⲏ — Greek παρεμβολή 'array, encampment' (orthographic variant of ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲟⲗⲏ in glossary; cf. plural ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲟⲗⲁⲩⲉ also in glossary). 'The array which I have proclaimed' refers to the cosmographic structure (5 watches × cosmic events) the apostle has just enumerated.

Translated as 'be in the likeness of' throughout (lines 5, 9, 13, 14, 15). Recurring Lyc. verb structurally parallel to ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲛⲧ̄ 'be likened' (lines 6, 15) and governing the same body-cosmos correspondence pattern. Possibly related to ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' giving 'be reckoned-as-like.' Preserves the correspondential identification in the rhetorical 'X is in the likeness of Y' formula. Proposed for vocabulary.
Translated 'steer (himself).' Lyc. ⲣ̄- + ⲍⲙ̄ⲙⲉ (= Sah. ϩⲙⲙⲉ 'steer, govern'). The reflexive ⲙⲙⲁϥ + directional ⲁⲡⲁⲅⲁⲑⲟⲛ 'toward the Good' fits standard nautical-moral usage 'steer oneself toward.'

Preserved as 'Phergokatochos.' Variant orthography of ⲫⲉⲣⲣⲟⲕⲁⲧⲟⲭⲟⲥ (in glossary, 'Bearer-Holder'), likely reflecting Greek φερρόκατοχος < φέρω + κατέχω. Same cosmic Holder figure standing above the Zone, matching the body-correspondence here at the level of the upper Zone (= the body's neck/throat region in the descending body-cosmos schema).

Parsed as ⲛ̄(ϥ-)ⲟⲃⲓⲟ-ϥ̄ '(and shall) make him be-in-likeness' = 'fashion him in (his) likeness.' The preceding ⲡⲉϩⲍⲏⲧ 'his heart' is the object being conformed to the heart's cosmic correspondent (the great King of Honor in the seventh heaven).

Translated 'sending forth upward to the heaven of Life.' ⲧⲛⲛⲁⲩ = standard Coptic 'send'; circumstantial ⲉϥ- yields 'while sending.' Fits the King of Glory's Manichaean role of conducting refined light upward via the cosmic wheels.

Preserved transliterated as 'Birah-Birē' — uncertain epithet. Possibly a doublet on ϥⲓ/ⲃⲓ 'bear, lift' yielding 'foot-bearer, (load-)bearer' as paired epithets of the Omophoros (here governing the binding of the archontic host below in the feet/soles register). Could alternatively be a Semitic loanword (Aramaic bīrā 'fortress,' giving 'Stronghold of Stronghold' as cosmic Atlas epithet). Proposed for vocabulary; flagged for parallels.

Translated 'his soles.' From Coptic ⲧⲏⲡⲥⲉ/ⲧⲉⲡⲥ 'heel, sole' with 3sg.m possessive Lyc. ⲡⲉϩ- (also written ⲛⲉϩ-). The body-correspondence at line-bottom register (= soles of feet) maps to ⲛⲛⲟⲩⲛ ⲉⲧⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'the Deep below' — direct cosmic-anatomical correspondence with the bottom pole of the cosmos.

Restored as ϣⲛⲍ̄ = Lyc. reduced form of ϣⲱⲛϩ̄/ⲱⲛϩ̄ 'live.' Translation 'lives' fits the context 'in which the man habitually lives in them' — the four virtues (love, joy, faith, truth) being the medium of human life. Editor's restoration of ⲛ accepted.
Translated 'truly, indeed.' Adverbial ⲙ̄ⲙⲉ (= ⲛ̄ⲙⲉ) intensifying the discourse-marker ⲧⲧⲁⲗⲓⲛ ⲁⲛ 'once again' — standard Kephalaia transition into a new exegetical frame.

Translated 'neck up to heaven.' ⲙⲟⲩⲧ here = 'neck' (Sah. ⲙⲟⲩⲧ), confirmed by line 5 ⲙ̄ⲡⲉϥⲙⲟⲩⲧ ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛ̄ 'from his neck downward.' This closes the description of the first cosmos (head/upper region), whose vertical extent runs from neck up to the crown ('heaven').

Translated 'place of seeing' — the visual organ. ⲓⲱⲣⲍ is the Lyc. equivalent of ⲱⲣϩ̄ 'see, watch' (cf. ⲣⲉϩⲓ̈ⲱⲣⲍ 'watcher, seer' in glossary). Forms a parallel series with ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ 'place of hearing,' ⲡⲙⲁⲛϣⲱⲗⲙ̄ 'place of smelling,' ⲡⲙⲁⲛⲭⲓⲧⲡⲉ 'place of receiving-taste.'

Translated 'his entire ϣⲁϣⲡⲉ' preserving transliteration. The lexeme is uncertain; possibly Lyc. for ϩⲉⲗⲡⲉ 'navel' (cf. ⲧⲉⲩϩⲁⲗⲡⲉ in glossary) or for ϣⲁϣⲧⲉ 'shaft/pillar.' Anatomically, the 2nd cosmos extends from neck to navel/lower-trunk, so 'navel' or 'midriff' is contextually likely.

Translated 'his two ears.' ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ is ambiguous between Lyc. forms of ⲙⲁⲁⲧϫⲉ/ⲙⲁⲥϫⲉ 'ear' and ⲙⲉⲥⲧⲉ 'breast.' Context decides: this paired feature in the FIRST cosmos (head) must be one of the head's pairs (eyes/ears/nostrils). The arms in the 2nd cosmos correspond to it; correspondence with ears (a paired projecting head-feature) is the most plausible. Note line 12 has ⲧⲙⲉⲥⲧ-ⲍⲏⲧ 'breast/midriff-of-heart' showing ⲙⲉⲥⲧ for breast — distinct from ⲙⲉϣⲧⲉ here.

Translated 'the two eyes of his heart.' ⲃⲉⲗ = Lyc. for ⲃⲁⲗ 'eye, opening, orifice.' Anatomically this likely refers to two cardiac chambers/atria (the heart's 'two eyes/openings'); literal 'eyes' is preserved to maintain the correspondential register. Together with the stomach, these complete the seven archons of the second cosmos (2 arms + 2 breasts + 2 cardiac-eyes + 1 stomach = 7).

Translated 'right between, between' as emphatic doubling. ⲟⲩⲧⲱϥ = 'between him/it' (preposition ⲟⲩⲧⲉ + 3sg.m suffix). The doubled relative clause likely intensifies the central position: 'precisely between' the two breasts, in the midriff.

Three abdominal organs preceding ⲡⲍⲏⲡⲁⲣ 'liver' and ⲡⲥⲓϣⲉ 'bile.' Preserved as transliterations. The standard Manichaean visceral inventory of seven would be heart/lungs/liver/spleen/gallbladder/kidneys/+1; since heart and stomach belong to the 2nd cosmos here, these likely include lungs and spleen with one other. Specific identifications: ⲡⲱⲧ possibly 'lungs' or 'back-organ'; ⲡⲟⲩⲁϥ literally 'the flesh' (= internal flesh-organ, possibly muscle/diaphragm); ⲡⲛⲁⲗⲱ possibly 'spleen.' All flagged.
Translated 'his two kidneys.' ⲟ̄ⲗⲱⲧ = Lyc. reflex of ϭⲗⲟⲧⲉ 'kidney.' The pairing as 'two' and position at end of 7-archon list (after liver and bile) confirms identification as kidneys.

Three pairs of leg-parts in the 4th (lower) cosmos. ⲕⲉⲍⲧⲉ = 'thighs/haunches' (per glossary). ⲧⲉⲧⲉ and ⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲧ are uncertain; possibly 'buttocks' and 'shins/calves' or 'hips' and 'knees.' The schema needs 6 paired body-parts + 1 generative member = 7. Preserved as transliterations.

Translated 'seed.' The relative clause 'from which the X comes forth, which begets all the forms' clearly indicates semen/seed. Etymology unclear; possibly Lyc. for ⲥⲡⲟⲣⲟⲥ/ⲥⲡⲉⲣⲙⲁ-equivalent, or related to a generative-emission verb.

Three qualitatives describing the zodiac signs' state in the celestial wheel. Tentatively 'stationed, fixed, placed' — three near-synonyms reinforcing their bound position in the cosmic structure. ⲧⲣⲁⲓ̈ⲧ possibly from a stand/set root; ⲁϥⲧ unclear (could be 'numbered' or 'sealed'); ⲭⲁⲓ̈ⲧ likely qualitative of ⲕⲱ/ⲭⲱ 'place, set.'

Translated 'they have been appointed, made into a circuit.' ⲧⲁϣⲟⲩ from ⲧⲱϣ 'appoint, fix' rather than ⲧⲁϣⲉ 'preach' — fits zodiacal-establishment context. ⲭⲱⲭ tentatively 'circuit/row/course' (possibly Lyc. for ϫⲱⲱϫⲉ 'row, course'), fitting the rotating zodiacal wheel imagery.

ⲕⲟ̄ⲛ unidentified; possibly Greek κανών 'rule, canon,' Greek κῶνος 'cone,' or Coptic ⲕⲱⲛ 'embrace, fellowship.' The construction ⲁ-ⲧⲣⲉ-ⲕⲟ̄ⲛ ⲧⲁⲡⲉ ⲛ̄[X] ⲛ̄ⲕⲟ̄ⲛ appears to express 'to make ⲕⲟ̄ⲛ a head of [X] of ⲕⲟ̄ⲛ' — possibly designating these zodiac-signs as the chief-rule/canon of some cosmic order. Preserved transliterated.

Tentatively 'the fire' = Lyc. ⲥⲉⲧ for ⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire' (cf. ⲡⲭⲁⲓ̈ ⲛⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'sun-ship of fire' in glossary). The contracted form without final -ⲉ is unusual but plausible. Alternative readings 'foundation' (ⲥⲛⲧⲉ) or 'tail' (ⲥⲏⲧ) less contextually probable. Confidence low.
Translated 'his neck' (not 'his sinew' as in earlier accumulated vocab). Sahidic ⲙⲟⲩⲧ has both meanings; here the body-part schema (head → neck → shoulders → arms) decisively requires 'neck.'

Translated 'his breast/chest.' The zodiacal mapping (Crab=breast in classical melothesia) confirms the body-part. Lycopolitan ϣⲁϣⲡⲉ is the breast/chest term, equivalent to standard Coptic ⲙⲉⲥⲧⲛⲍⲏⲧ in this register.
Translated 'the bone of his loin.' ⲝⲓⲥⲉ = Lyc. ϫⲓⲥⲉ; here body-part 'loin/lower-back.' The zodiacal mapping (Libra=loin/hip area) confirms.

Translated 'his thighs.' Body-part term filling the slot between Scorpio (groin) and Capricorn (knees), which canonical melothesia assigns to the thighs (Sagittarius). The exact lexical root remains uncertain.
Translated 'the calves of his legs.' ⲥⲛϩⲉ likely Lyc. for 'calf-tendon/calf'; ⲣⲉⲧ⸗ = 'foot/leg.' Aquarius governs the calves in standard melothesia.
Translated 'the soles of his feet.' ⲟⲁⲡ likely Lyc. for ⲱⲡ/ⲟⲩⲡ 'sole.' Pisces governs the feet — confirmed.

Translated 'the twelve zodiac-(creatures).' ⲍⲱ here = Greek ζῷον, used in Manichaean cosmology for the twelve zodiacal animals (cf. ⲍⲱⲇⲟⲛ in glossary). Line break truncates the word; restored sense is unambiguous.
Translated 'the foundation' from ⲥⲛⲧⲉ 'foundation.' The body 'head against foundation' = head/feet polarity, the full vertical extent.
Translated 'his ankle.' ⲧⲡⲉ here likely = ⲧⲏⲡⲉ 'ankle/extremity' rather than ⲧⲡⲉ 'top.' Confirmed by symmetric phrasing line 27 'from his ankle up to his head' — clearly the lower extremity.

Translated tentatively 'the right side-of-the-head.' The right-half enumeration must begin with the head-region (Aries=head in the full schema). The exact lexeme ⲥⲙⲉⲩ is obscure; possibly = 'temple' or 'right brow.' Flagged as proposed term.

Translated tentatively 'the left-hip-region.' Position in left-half enumeration before Scorpio (left-rib) suggests the Libra-corresponding hip/loin region of the left side. Possibly compound: ϩⲃⲟⲩⲣ 'left' + ⲍⲟⲩⲛ/ⲁⲥⲟⲩⲛ 'inner.' Etymology uncertain.

Greek zodiac names retained in Coptic transcription. ὑδροχόος = Aquarius (water-pourer); ἰχθύς = Pisces (fish). The kephalaion maps body parts of a cosmic figure (probably the body of man as microcosm) to zodiac signs. Translated by zodiacal name to preserve technical reference.

Body-part term of uncertain identification, paired with 'left' as in line 1's 'left tooth.' Could be Lycopolitan for a facial feature (jaw, eyebrow, ear, lip). Translated as 'X' / placeholder rather than guessing; the term is physically present in the manuscript so kept inline rather than in apparatus.

Greek δημιουργός 'demiurge, fashioner.' Used here for the cosmic fashioner of the body — the archonic agent who multiplied the powers within. Retained as 'demiurge' to preserve the Manichaean technical sense of dark cosmic craftsman.

'800 and 40 myriads' = 8,400,000. Combined with line 11's '210 myriads' = 2,100,000 houses, the math (8,400,000 ÷ 4 archons-per-house = 2,100,000 houses) confirms the four-by-four schema. Numbers translated literally to preserve the arithmetical-cosmological precision.

Translated 'crying out' from ϣⲗ-stem (related to outcry/uproar). Alternative readings 'praying' (from ϣⲗⲏⲗ) or 'raging' are possible. The martial-incursive context (archons fighting one another within the body) supports an aggressive vocalizing sense. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'rebuke' as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲃ 'answer back, contradict' or related to ⲱⲃϣ̄ 'shame.' Confidence moderate; the verb is in a sequence of mutual-injury verbs (rebuke / destroy / [act]).

Lexeme of uncertain identification; tentatively translated 'matter' (corruption, noxious substance from a wound) on contextual grounds — the surrounding language describes a wound being drawn out and treated medically. Etymology unclear; possibly related to a body-fluid or wound-substance term.

Translated 'drawn forth' (from ⲡⲱⲣⲕ̄ in the sense 'extract, uproot' — cf. accumulated vocabulary). The medical-anatomical context (extraction in the wound, followed by therapeutic treatment) confirms this sense over the alternate 'swear an oath.'

Reduplicated form, tentatively 'scraping' from ⲕⲱϩⲕⲉϩ — a medical-surgical scraping or rubbing treatment. The Greek loanword ⲑⲉⲣⲁⲡⲉⲩⲉ 'apply therapy' immediately following supports the medical register.

Translated 'soothe (it) out' as a tentative healing/easing verb; the directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth' on line 24 confirms a verb of expulsion/release. Etymology uncertain; could alternatively be 'expel' or 'cure.'
